lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wake up to the smell of smoke in the air. Looking around, you are startled to see that the grove is engulfed in flames. The house roof is still destroyed, the elf is desperately trying to put out the fire with the polluted pond water with little success, and the garden is in shambles.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In his panicked state, the elf meets your gaze. He looks at you with a face of anger, but continues in his futile efforts. You look around for the fae, who is cackling to herself near the gate which is now fully melted down. The fae turns toward you with a smug grin, clearly pleased with herself.

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: Well, would you look at that—you actually helped me escape. It was taking forever for me to break all those locks myself, but now the barrier is destroyed and I’m free!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She starts laughing again.

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: It’s honestly hilarious! While that elf was busy thinking you were trying to help restore his precious grove, you were tearing it apart for me instead. You broke the locks, drained the pond, and took away what little remained of the grove’s resources. Exactly what I wanted and now we’re both free!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fae lets out another amused giggle, clearly delighted with herself.

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: Well, this has been fun. I’m sure the elf will be absolutely delighted when he realizes what you’ve done. As for me, since I have a human world to return to, I have far more exciting plans in store. Thanks for the help, try not to miss me too much!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She gives you one last smug grin before disappearing through the gate, her laughter fading into the distance and leaving you alone. You want to leave too, but can’t help looking back at the devastation. You know that this is your fault, but what can you do now? You can’t stay for long, the smoke is getting to your head. So you exit through the gate and escape the enchanted grove.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wake up and head over to the gate. The elf is already there, waiting for you.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Although you have not successfully completed all of my requests, I will fulfill my promise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He inspects the remaining locks carefully.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Strange, it seems that some of these locks are destroyed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He looks at you, pausing and contemplating his next action. He sighs.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Well I suppose I did tell you that I will unlock as many locks as tasks you have completed for me. Very well, I will unlock the remaining locks for you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The elf takes out a keyring from his pocket and unlocks whatever locks remained. The gate opens up.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Alright, hurry along now. It seems that I will need to replace these locks somehow. Although I can let you out, I must maintain the barrier so evil spirits don’t escape the grove into the human world. I hope you didn’t run into any of those during your stay here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You approach the gate, but before you head out, you look around your surroundings. In the corner of your eye, you can see the fae watching you from a distance with an annoyed expression. The elf seems to be impatiently waiting for you to leave. So you exit through the gate and escape the enchanted grove.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wake up and head over to the gate. The elf is already there, waiting for you. He looks around the grove with a rare smile, taking in the scene. He turns toward you.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: You have done an excellent job. I must admit, when you first arrived, this grove was in a sorry state. But thanks to your efforts, it is already beginning to look like the place it once was. My house is all fixed up, the pond is clean, and the animals now have food to rely on. You have my sincerest thanks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He gives you a proud nod, his usual sternness replaced by genuine appreciation.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: You have proven yourself to be a great help to this grove, and I am grateful for everything you have done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Unbeknownst to the elf, the fae watches from a distance between the trees, her expression darkening as she listens. Her hands curl into fists, her eyes fixed angrily on you as she seethes with frustration.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Please consider this grove a place you may call upon whenever you need it. I will still need to maintain the barrier to keep some evil spirits inside the grove, but please do not view its existence as a deterrent. You are always welcome here, should you ever wish to return, just write the message on a leaf and it will carry it to me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The elf bows toward you with open palms. You carefully bow back, trying to imitate his pose. You want to stay in the grove for just a bit longer, but you know that, for now, you must go. So you exit through the gate and escape the enchanted grove.
